2608.03529.title: Consensus Measures for Unstructured Biomedical Text Annotations
2608.03529.paper_summary: Biomedical literature is increasingly mined for knowledge beyond the questions it was written to answer. Because the target concepts are not known in advance, annotators prefer open-ended labels, whose agreement is hard to quantify. We study soft inter-rater reliability for annotators providing unstructured texts for biomedical annotation tasks. Synthetic experiments show that soft reliability can be quantified using a variety of semantic equivalence measures, and that the choice of measure affects failure modes of the estimation. Embeddings are scalable, but limited when differentiating similar but distinct concepts. Large language models are promising, but limited by scalability for estimating agreement by chance. Finally, we suggest measures based on natural language inference as a sensible compromise.
2608.03529.paper_summary_zh: 生物醫學文獻越來越多地被挖掘以獲取超越其原本問題的知識。因為目標概念事先並不明確，標註者更喜歡開放式標籤，而這種標籤的協議性難以量化。我們研究了為生物醫學標註任務提供非結構化文本的標註者的軟性評分者可靠性。合成實驗顯示，軟性可靠性可以使用多種語義等價度量來量化，且度量的選擇會影響估計的失敗模式。嵌入技術具有可擴展性，但在區分相似但不同的概念時受到限制。大型語言模型前景看好，但在估計隨機一致性方面受到可擴展性的限制。最後，我們建議基於自然語言推理的度量作為一種合理的折衷方案。
